Notes.Text:
This update for google-osconfig-agent fixes the following issues:

- CVE-2026-61801: github.com/moby/sys/user: unbounded parsing of user and group database files can lead to denial of
  service (bsc#1284870).
- CVE-2026-78659: golang.org/x/net/http2: HTTP/2 server memory exhaustion due to Trailer headers (bsc#1286994).
- CVE-2026-78660: golang.org/x/net/http2: HTTP/2 transport accepts malformed framing-related headers (bsc#1287058).
- CVE-2026-78661: golang.org/x/net/html: quadratic complexity when coalescing text nodes (bsc#1289368).
- CVE-2026-78663: golang.org/x/net/http2: double flow control refund on HTTP/2 server streams (bsc#1287137).
- CVE-2026-78669: golang.org/x/net/http2: excessive CPU consumption from repeated initial window changes (bsc#1285283).
- CVE-2026-79775: github.com/diskfs/go-diskfs: malformed SquashFS image can cause crashes and persistent CPU loops in
  rclone's archive backend (bsc#1278163).
- CVE-2026-95838: github.com/containerd/containerd: processing of certain image layers causes superlinear time
  complexity in unpack handler and can lead to DoS (bsc#1285135).
- CVE-2026-97032: golang.org/x/net/http2: HTTP/2 server crash due to HPACK encoder race (bsc#1287487).
- CVE-2026-97045: golang.org/x/net/html: missing checks can cause parser to resolve a subtree in a different foreign
  namespace upon re-parsing rendered output (bsc#1289424).
- CVE-2026-109425: github.com/tink-crypto/tink-go/v2/keyset: missing structural validation in NewHandleWithNoSecrets()
  allows malformed public keysets (bsc#1285110).
- CVE-2026-116585,CVE-2026-116586,CVE-2026-116587: github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v4: multiple security issues in
  github.com/go-jose/go-jose before 4.1.6 (bsc#1288375).
- CVE-2026-116591: github.com/klauspost/compress/zstd: crafted ~27 KB two-block zstd frame makes DecodeAll and the
  streaming decoder panic (bsc#1288461).

Changes for google-osconfig-agent:

- Update to version 20261105.03:
  * E2E tests v2 redesign: migrate PackageResource Googet tests (#1073)
  * Fix race between osconfig reboot and Windows TrustedInstaller reboot (#1082)
  * E2E tests v2 redesign: migrate PackageResource Msi tests (#1074)
  * E2E V2: Migrate guest policy package repository case (#1058)
  * E2E tests v2 redesign: migrate PackageResource Yum tests (#1068)
  * E2E tests v2 redesign: migrate PackageResource Deb tests (#1063)
  * e2e v2: migrate os patch job execution (#1061)
  * E2E tests v2 redesign: migrate RepositoryResource Apt tests (#1075)
  * Add unit tests for zypper.go (#1014)
  * Add unit tests for util/util.go (#995)
  * Add scalibr flow for windows (#1037)
  * Add scalibr os benchmarks (#1044)

Vulnerabilities.Description: Tink-go (tink-crypto/tink-go) through 2.8.0 contains an input-validation vulnerability where keyset.NewHandleWithNoSecrets() and ReadWithNoSecrets() skip the structural Validate() step before constructing a keyset.Handle, allowing malformed public or no-secret keysets that violate Tink's keyset invariants to be accepted. Attackers can supply a malformed keyset, such as one with an enabled public key lacking a valid primary key or a DESTROYED key with no KeyData, causing inconsistent downstream validation where functions like jwt.JWKSetFromPublicKeysetHandle() process the invalid handle and produce a JWK set, potentially misleading applications that rely on successful handle construction as proof of keyset integrity.

Vulnerabilities.Description: Go JOSE provides an implementation of the Javascript Object Signing and Encryption set of standards in Go, including support for JSON Web Encryption (JWE), JSON Web Signature (JWS), and JSON Web Token (JWT) standards. Prior to 4.1.5, decrypting untrusted JWE ciphertext with A128CBC-HS256, A192CBC-HS384, or A256CBC-HS512 can pass an empty ciphertext buffer to CBC-HMAC unpadding. Insufficient validation allows the empty buffer to be indexed, causing a panic and denial of service. Applications that decrypt attacker-controlled ciphertext with one of these content-encryption algorithms are affected. This issue is fixed in version 4.1.5.

Prior to 4.1.5, parsing attacker-controlled JSON through go-jose allows deeply nested arrays or objects to exceed Go's stack limit. The resulting stack overflow crashes the application and permits denial of service in applications that parse untrusted JSON through go-jose. This issue is fixed in version 4.1.5.

Vulnerabilities.Description: Go JOSE provides an implementation of the Javascript Object Signing and Encryption set of standards in Go, including support for JSON Web Encryption (JWE), JSON Web Signature (JWS), and JSON Web Token (JWT) standards. Prior to 4.1.6, go-jose parses attacker-controlled RSA modulus and prime values from JWKs without enforcing size and consistency bounds before passing them to crypto/rsa.PrivateKey.Validate. On Go 1.24 and later, crafted large or degenerate RSA parameters can make that validation consume cubic CPU time, allowing remote denial of service in applications that parse JWKs from untrusted sources. This issue is fixed in version 4.1.6.

Vulnerabilities.Description: compress provides various compression algorithms. Prior to 1.20.2, the zstd DecodeAll and streaming decoder paths can panic when a crafted two-block frame reaches huff0.ReadTable with an FSE normalized count of 32768 that readNCount stores in int16 as -32768. The wrapped count allows buildDtable to retain stale fse.Scratch decode-table state from the prior block, and nextFast then derives an out-of-range state and indexes beyond the table instead of returning a decode error. Both blocks are required to preserve and then reuse the stale state, allowing untrusted zstd input to crash an application. This issue is fixed in version 1.20.2.

Vulnerabilities.Description: The `github.com/moby/sys/user` package provides Go utilities for parsing and looking up entries in Unix-style user and group database files. Versions before 0.4.1 do not sufficiently limit entries when parsing `/etc/passwd`- or `/etc/group`-style files, allowing an attacker who can supply a specially crafted file to cause excessive memory consumption and potentially terminate the affected process due to an out-of-memory condition. This issue is patched in version 0.4.1. As a workaround, avoid parsing attacker-controlled user or group database files, or validate and limit untrusted input before parsing it.

Vulnerabilities.Description: When "Trailer" headers are sent by a client, the HTTP server internally uses the header values to populate the Request.Trailer map passed to the server handler. Because Request.Trailer is a map, each entry incurs memory overhead. For HTTP/2 servers, a malicious client can exploit this by sending a "Trailer" header that declares a large number of fields, causing the server to allocate a disproportionate amount of memory while bypassing Server.MaxHeaderValueCount and Server.MaxHeaderBytes limits. This exploit is not applicable for HTTP/1 servers, which do not support multiplexing a large number of requests over one TCP connection, and whose Server.MaxHeaderBytes are calculated differently.

Vulnerabilities.Description: Historically, we have been rather lax about malformed framing-related headers in our HTTP/2 implementation, as they cannot interfere with HTTP/2 framing. However, this makes it possible for our HTTP/2 implementation to forward responses containing such headers to an HTTP/1 client when acting as a reverse proxy. If the HTTP/1 client also does not behave strictly enough, this can result in response smuggling.

Vulnerabilities.Description: When coalescing adjacent text nodes in addText and fosterParent, appending to an existing TextNode's Data via string concatenation (n.Data += text) reallocated and copied the accumulated string on every token. Inputs containing many short text runs separated by ignored end tags (such as "a</x>") caused O(n^2) allocations and byte copies. Accumulate coalesced text in per-node byte slices during parsing and materialize Data strings once at the end of parse.

Vulnerabilities.Description: The HTTP/2 server can refund connection-level flow control twice for the same data: Once when a client resets a stream (refunding data for any sent-but-unread portion of the stream), and again when a request handler reads the buffered data. A malicious client can exploit this to bypass the configured connection-level flow control limit (MaxReceiveBufferPerConnection). Total buffered data is still limited by the concurrent stream limit and stream-level flow control.

Vulnerabilities.Description: rclone versions >= v1.72.0 and <= v1.74.4 (fixed in v1.75.0) contain multiple denial-of-service vulnerabilities in the archive backend's SquashFS parser, which relies on the github.com/diskfs/go-diskfs dependency. The parser fails to validate attacker-controlled superblock and metadata values before use. An attacker who can place or modify a SquashFS image in storage exposed through an rclone :archive: remote can craft a malicious image that triggers an integer division-by-zero panic (zero block size), an out-of-bounds slice panic (out-of-range inode metadata offset), or a non-progress CPU loop (truncated metadata stream). Variants 1 and 2 terminate the rclone process and, via 'rclone serve sftp', can crash the entire SFTP server; variant 3 causes sustained CPU consumption. Parsing is lazy, so a victim or remote client must address or descend into the malicious archive object to trigger it.

Vulnerabilities.Description: containerd is an open-source container runtime. Prior to 1.7.35, 2.0.12, 2.2.8, and 2.3.5, containerd's layer unpack handler repeatedly traverses directories for certain opaque whiteout configurations. A malicious image layer can trigger repeated directory traversals while opaque whiteouts are processed. Pulling or importing the image can consume CPU, delay container startup, and reduce image-pull concurrency for unrelated deployments. This issue is fixed in versions 1.7.35, 2.0.12, 2.2.8, and 2.3.5.

Vulnerabilities.Description: HTTP/2 servers could end up crashing due to inadvertently modifying its HPACK encoder concurrently. This happens because the server modifies the HPACK encoder from two goroutines without synchronization: one uses the encoder to encode a HEADERS frame as part of a response sent to a client and the other modifies the encoder's table size when handling a SETTINGS frame containing SETTINGS_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE that a client sends. A malicious client can repeatedly send a request while changing the header table size to crash the server.

Vulnerabilities.Description: In childTextNodesAreLiteral, walking up the tree previously stopped at the nearest foreign ancestor once an HTML integration point was found. However, that integration point may itself be a descendant of an element that was foster-parented into a foreign namespace (such as <mglyph> or <malignmark> fostered under <mtext>), causing a parser to resolve the subtree in a different foreign namespace upon re-parsing the rendered output. Continue walking the full ancestor chain and verify that every transition from a non-empty namespace occurs at an HTML integration point before emitting literal text.
